summary: This Snowflake documentation page explains bind variables, which replace literal values in SQL statements with placeholders filled in by application code, helping prevent SQL injection. It covers placeholder syntax (?, :varname, %varname), use with drivers, Snowflake Scripting, and the SQL API, and describes array binds for batch inserts with their limitations. It also shows how to bind semi-structured data into VARIANT columns.
one_line: Snowflake documentation on using bind variables in SQL statements, including placeholder syntax, array binds for batch inserts, and semi-structured data.
key_facts: Bind variables let an application put placeholders in a SQL statement and supply the values separately, and they can prevent SQL injection attacks when user input is used.
Placeholder syntax is either ? , :<varname>, or %<varname>, depending on the programming language.
In Snowflake Scripting, a bind variable is prefixed with a colon, as in INSERT INTO t (c1) VALUES (:variable1).
The PHP driver does not support bind variables.
The PHP driver does not support array binds.
An array bind, also called a bulk insert or batch insert, can improve performance by inserting multiple rows in a single batch, avoiding network round trips and compilations.
In the Python array bind example, conn.cursor().executemany is called with the bind list [('milk', 2), ('apple', 3), ('egg', 2)] to insert three rows into the grocery table.
Only INSERT INTO … VALUES statements can contain array bind variables.
The VALUES clause for an array bind must be a single-row list of bind variables; VALUES (?,?), (?,?) is not allowed.
INSERT INTO t VALUES (?,?), (?,?) inserts exactly four values without using an array bind, using the bind list [1,'String1',2,'String2'].
To bind semi-structured data, the variable is bound as a string and parsed with PARSE_JSON in the INSERT statement.
Snowflake supports other data loading methods that are recommended instead of using array binds.
The statement INSERT INTO t SELECT ARRAY_CONSTRUCT(column1) FROM VALUES (?) inserts an array of semi-structured data into a VARIANT column with a bind variable.
